name: Head Cleanup
description: Trim WordPress's default `<head>` to what modern sites actually use — drop feed / oEmbed / shortlink discovery tags, strip stylesheet boilerplate, kill the s.w.org DNS-prefetch hint.

sections.title: <head> bloat
sections.description: Remove the `wp_head` actions WordPress hangs on for legacy clients (feed readers, RSD, oEmbed clients) that nobody actually uses anymore.

settings.label: Disable feed discovery
settings.description: Removes the `<link rel=alternate>` RSS / Atom feed tags from every page. Site feeds still work directly; they just aren't advertised.

settings.label: Disable RSD / WLW manifest
settings.description: Drops the Really Simple Discovery + Windows Live Writer endpoint tags. Both are 2005-era remote-editing protocols.

settings.label: Disable relational link tags
settings.description: Removes the `<link rel=index / parent / start / prev / next>` post-relation tags. Useful only to a handful of feed crawlers.

settings.label: Hide WordPress identity
settings.description: Removes the `<meta name=generator>` (your WP version), the `<link rel=shortlink>`, and the `<link rel=https://api.w.org/>` REST discovery link. Drops a small fingerprinting surface.

settings.label: Disable oEmbed discovery
settings.description: Removes the oEmbed discovery `<link>` + host JS WordPress adds so other sites can embed your posts. Disabling doesn't stop you embedding *other* sites' content.

settings.label: Disable Recent Comments widget CSS
settings.description: Removes the inline `<style>` block the Recent Comments widget injects. Safe to leave on even if the widget isn't used.
